newsitem.title: USA: Stiglitz sees inflation stable, room for wage gain.
newsitem.headline: Stiglitz sees inflation stable, room for wage gain.

text.p: U.S. inflation remains stable and the possibility of a jump in inflation is remote, Joseph Stiglitz, chairman of the White House Council of Economic Advisers, said Monday.
"Inflation remains stable ... there is room for a sustained increase in real wages," Stiglitz said in remarks to the press during a Chicago Board of Trade economic outlook panel presentation here.
The present economic expansion is supported by high consumer confidence, high housing starts, high income growth and strong business investment, Stiglitz said.
"Expansions do not die of old age," Stiglitz said, suggesting that past expansions have been throttled by anti-inflationary government measures.
"This expansion ... will continue through 1997 and beyond," he said.
